                    ### Question
                    A 22-year-old female presents at 24 weeks gestation with a chief complaint of burning upon urination. On physical exam, you note a gravid uterus that extends above the umbilicus. A urine analysis and culture is sent demonstrating over 100,000 colony forming units of E. coli. Of note this patient had a similar UTI 7 weeks ago that was resolved with appropriate medication. Which of the following is the most appropriate management of this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Nitrofurantoin
opb. TMP-SMX
opc. Cephalexin
opd. Nitrofurantoin and continue with nitrofurantoin prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy
ope. Cephalexin and IV antibiotic prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
A 22-year-old female at 24 weeks gestation presents with burning upon urination and a urine culture showing >100,000 CFU of E. coli, indicating a urinary tract infection (UTI). Given her history of a similar UTI 7 weeks ago, recurrent UTIs are common in pregnancy. The management of UTIs in pregnant patients must prioritize safety for both the mother and fetus. Nitrofurantoin and Cephalexin are both considered safe options during pregnancy, while TMP-SMX is less preferred, especially in the first trimester due to potential risks. Prophylactic treatment with Nitrofurantoin can help prevent recurrence. Therefore, the most appropriate management for this patient is Nitrofurantoin with prophylaxis for the remainder of the pregnancy, as it effectively treats the current infection and reduces the risk of future UTIs.
